# Aircraft systems {#sec-aircraft-systems}

This note describes the aircraft systems corpus for an operator. It states
what the corpus is, the runtime fields it feeds, how it refreshes, the
licence rules, the engine ceiling per system and the non-goals.

## What the corpus is

The systems corpus gives every supported AEE air class a source-backed
real-world specification. The corpus holds the only real aircraft values. The
game config is identity evidence.

The corpus is a shared foundation. The aircraft family is the first consumer.
The land family is a branch. Read `data/aircraft/INDEX.md` for the layers and
`data/vehicle/SCHEMA.md` sections 16 and 17 for the shared contract and the
land physics surface.

The systems fields sit beside the four-value flight-model row. The four-value
row is unchanged. The systems fields get a second lookup.

## The runtime fields it feeds

The generator `tools/validation/gen_aircraft_systems.py` writes
`addons/flight/functions/fnc_getAircraftSystems.sqf`. The row is fixed
order. A consumer indexes by name.

- Fuel: `fuel_capacity`, `fuel_consumption_rate`, `fuel_density_kg_l`,
  `sfc_kg_kwh`, `fuel_cg_arm_m`.
- Engine: `engine_design_rpm`, `engine_idle_ng`, `engine_max_ng`,
  `engine_max_np`, `engine_max_torque_nm`, `engine_max_tgt_c`,
  `engine_oil_pressure_min_kpa`, `engine_oil_pressure_max_kpa`,
  `transmission_torque_limit_nm`.
- Status: `hydraulic_pressure_kpa`, `generator_power_kw`, `bus_voltage_v`,
  `battery_capacity_ah`, `cabin_pressure_max_kpa`.
- Enums: `fuel_type`, `engine_oil_type`, `oxygen_system`.

The load-time config projection `tools/validation/gen_physics_config.py`
writes `fuelCapacity`, `fuelConsumptionRate`, `mass` and the centre of gravity
into the one `CfgVehicles` block. The engine burn is set to zero, so the
sourced rate drives a scripted burn and the two never double-count.

One per-frame driver, `fnc_updateAircraftSystems.sqf`, schedules the four
kernels: fuel, engine, damage and status.

## How it refreshes

Run one command from the repository root:

```
tools/build_aircraft_data.sh
```

The script validates the corpus, regenerates the coverage, the two runtime
projections and the load-time config, then runs every freshness gate. A stale
generated file fails the build.

The individual commands are:

- `python3 tools/validation/validate_aircraft_data.py`, the provenance gate.
- `python3 tools/validation/gen_aircraft_coverage.py`, the coverage and gaps.
- `python3 tools/validation/gen_aircraft_data.py`, the four-value projection.
- `python3 tools/validation/gen_aircraft_systems.py`, the systems lookup.
- `python3 tools/validation/gen_physics_config.py`, the load-time config.

Each writer has a `--check` mode. It writes nothing and exits 1 on a stale
file. Fetching a new source document is a separate act. Use
`python3 tools/validation/fetch_vehicle_sources.py --data-dir data/aircraft
<source_id>` when the digest is pinned.

## The licence rules

The reference mods (Project Hatchet H-60 and BradMick's HeliSim) and RHS, CUP
and DCS are No-Derivatives or structure-only. Only their structure is
learnable. No number is copied from a No-Derivatives source.

Every number comes from a primary published source: a flight manual, a
pilot's operating handbook, a type certificate data sheet, a standard or a
maker datasheet. A proprietary or unheld document is a lead, not a value
source. A class with no real counterpart is recorded as `no_source`.

A fictional Arma class binds to a real analogue at grade `claimed`, because
no published source names a fictional class. The catalogue entry the binding
points to carries held-source values at grade `documented`, and a tier 5
compilation is never a value source. A family with no held analogue stays
`no_source` with a reason that names the exact next source and its licence.
`docs/adr/ADR-039-aircraft-analogue-sourcing.md` records the rule and the
licence boundary.

## The engine ceiling per system

- Fuel: built-in partial. `fuelCapacity`, `fuelConsumptionRate` and `setFuel`
  exist. The transfer, the jettison and the centre-of-gravity shift are
  scripted.
- Engine: the engine exposes `setWantedRPMRTD` and the RotorLib real-time data
  getters only when `difficultyEnabledRTD` is true. The kernel commands
  `setWantedRPMRTD [rpm, seconds, engineIndex]` with the published
  `engine_design_rpm` as the base and a `getEngineTargetRPMRTD` fallback when
  the base is absent. Turbine temperature, oil, start and wear are not exposed
  and are scripted.
- Damage: built-in. `HitPoints`, `get` and `setHitPointDamage`, `setDamage`
  and `allowDamage` exist. The per-system progressive damage is scripted.
- Status systems: absent. Hydraulics, electrical and pressurisation are status
  only. They never feed the flight dynamics model.
- The flight dynamics model is engine-fixed at config load. There is no
  runtime model swap.
- Land: the tyre and contact solver, the gearbox shift logic, the suspension
  and the engine-power curve are engine-owned. AEE owns only bounded force
  deltas on the owner machine and never calls `setVelocity` on a driven
  vehicle.

The scripted magnitude is a residual the operator signs. It is not a gate.

## Non-goals

- No number copied from an APL-ND, APL-SA, APL, CC-BY-NC-ND or GRAD source.
- No DCS number. DCS is a reference for what to model, never a data source.
- No runtime flight-model swap and no blade-element replacement.
- No engine XML for a land vehicle.
- No `setVelocity` on a driven vehicle.
- No invented analogue for a class with no real counterpart.
- No new PBO and no config value used as a real figure.
